summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis, grade I esophageal varices, and chronic pain was admitted for evaluation of melena and lightheadedness. Initial labs showed stable hemoglobin and elevated white count, which resolved without infection. An EGD revealed grade I varices without active bleeding but was limited by food in the stomach; gastric and duodenal mucosa appeared normal. Colonoscopy showed no lower GI source. A capsule endoscopy was performed to evaluate the small bowel for occult bleeding. Liver ultrasound confirmed cirrhosis without new lesions or vascular thrombosis. The patient remained hemodynamically stable, with mild hemoglobin drop attributed to possible chronic GI blood loss. Diuretics were resumed, and she was discharged home with stable vital signs, instructions to follow up on capsule results, and continuation of liver-protective and GI-protective medications.
problems: Unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma
Esophageal varices in diseases classified elsewhere, without mention of bleeding
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, unspecified
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
